chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad) from Al-Abbas ibn Amir from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zur'ah who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "I'tikaf (spiritual retreat) is not valid except with fasting."
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And there is no I'tikaf for less than three days."

key_terms.الاعْتِكَافُ: I'tikaf, spiritual retreat in a mosque

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the validity of I'tikaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* establishes fasting as a strict prerequisite for the validity of I'tikaf, reflecting the juristic consensus that the spiritual retreat is an extension of the devotional state of fasting. The appended note by Shaykh al-Tusi specifies a minimum duration of three days, distinguishing this practice from brief, informal stays and emphasizing its status as a sustained act of worship. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the structural integrity of ritual acts, linking physical discipline (fasting) with temporal commitment (duration) to ensure spiritual focus.
